patches.old:
I asked, “What is the tower?” He said, “The tower is the church.”

2. I asked, “Who are these virgins?” He said, “They are holy spirits.[a] No one can be found in God’s kingdom unless they clothe that person in their garment. Receiving only the name will do you no good if you do not also receive their garment. These virgins are powers of the Son of God. If you bear his name but do not wear his power, you bear his name in vain.”

3. “The stones you saw cast out are people who bore the name but did not put on the virgins’ clothing.” I asked, “What is their clothing, sir?” He said, “Their names are their clothing. Whoever bears the name of the Son of God must also bear their names. The Son himself bears these virgins’ names.”

4. “All the stones you saw enter the tower’s building, pass through their hands and remain in the building are clothed in the power of these virgins.”[b]

5. “That is why the tower has become one stone with the rock.[c] Those who have believed in the Lord through his Son and put on these spirits will become one spirit and one body. Their garments will have one color. People who bear the virgins’ names have their dwelling in the tower.”

6. I asked, “Then why, sir, were the rejected stones cast out? They passed through the gate. The virgins’ hands placed them in the tower’s building.” He said, “Everything concerns you, and you examine it closely. Listen to the explanation about the rejected stones.”

7. “They all received the name of the Son of God and the virgins’ power. These spirits strengthened them. They were with God’s servants and had one spirit, one body and one garment.[d] They thought the same things and practiced righteousness.”

8. “Later, the women you saw persuaded them. These women wore black garments, had bare shoulders and loose hair, and were beautiful. The people desired them. They put on the women’s power and took off the virgins’ power.”

9. “They were cast out of God’s house and handed over to those women. But those who were not deceived by their beauty stayed in God’s house. Now you have the explanation about those cast out.”[e]

translation:
  text: '“And what is the tower?” I said. “This tower is the church,” he said.


    2. “Who are these virgins?” “They are holy spirits,” he said.[a] “A person cannot otherwise be found
    in God’s kingdom unless they clothe that person in their garment. For if you receive only the name,
    but do not receive the garment from them, you will gain nothing. These virgins are powers of the Son
    of God. So if you bear his name but do not wear his power, you will bear his name in vain.”


    3. “The stones you saw cast out,” he said, “are people who bore the name but did not put on the virgins’
    clothing.” “What is their clothing, sir?” I said. “Their very names are their clothing,” he said.
    “Whoever bears the name of the Son of God must also bear their names, for the Son himself bears the
    names of these virgins.”


    4. “All the stones you saw entering the building of the tower, handed over through their hands and
    remaining in the building, are clothed in the power of these virgins.”[b]


    5. “That is why you see that the tower has become a single stone with the rock.[c] In the same way,
    those who have believed in the Lord through his Son and put on these spirits will become one spirit
    and one body, and their garments will have one color. Those who bear the virgins’ names have their
    dwelling in the tower.”


    6. “Then why, sir,” I said, “were the rejected stones cast out? They passed through the gate and were
    placed in the building of the tower through the virgins’ hands.” “Since everything concerns you,”
    he said, “and you examine it closely, listen about the rejected stones.”


    7. “They all received the name of the Son of God and the power of these virgins. On receiving these
    spirits, they were strengthened. They were with God’s servants, and they had one spirit, one body
    and one garment,[d] for they thought the same things and practiced righteousness.”


    8. “After some time, however, they were persuaded by the women you saw dressed in black garments,
    with bare shoulders and loose hair, who were beautiful. On seeing these women, they desired them and
    put on their power, but took off the virgins’ power.”


    9. “So they were cast out of God’s house and handed over to those women. But those who were not deceived
    by the beauty of these women remained in God’s house. Now you have the explanation about those who
    were cast out.”[e]'

translation:
  text: 'I asked, “What is the tower?” He said, “The tower is the church.”


    2. I asked, “Who are these virgins?” He said, “They are holy spirits.[a] No one can be found in God’s
    kingdom unless they clothe that person in their garment. Receiving only the name will do you no good
    if you do not also receive their garment. These virgins are powers of the Son of God. If you bear
    his name but do not wear his power, you bear his name in vain.”


    3. “The stones you saw cast out are people who bore the name but did not put on the virgins’ clothing.”
    I asked, “What is their clothing, sir?” He said, “Their names are their clothing. Whoever bears the
    name of the Son of God must also bear their names. The Son himself bears these virgins’ names.”


    4. “All the stones you saw enter the tower’s building, pass through their hands and remain in the
    building are clothed in the power of these virgins.”[b]


    5. “That is why the tower has become one stone with the rock.[c] Those who have believed in the Lord
    through his Son and put on these spirits will become one spirit and one body. Their garments will
    have one color. People who bear the virgins’ names have their dwelling in the tower.”


    6. I asked, “Then why, sir, were the rejected stones cast out? They passed through the gate. The virgins’
    hands placed them in the tower’s building.” He said, “Everything concerns you, and you examine it
    closely. Listen to the explanation about the rejected stones.”


    7. “They all received the name of the Son of God and the virgins’ power. These spirits strengthened
    them. They were with God’s servants and had one spirit, one body and one garment.[d] They thought
    the same things and practiced righteousness.”


    8. “Later, the women you saw persuaded them. These women wore black garments, had bare shoulders and
    loose hair, and were beautiful. The people desired them. They put on the women’s power and took off
    the virgins’ power.”


    9. “They were cast out of God’s house and handed over to those women. But those who were not deceived
    by their beauty stayed in God’s house. Now you have the explanation about those cast out.”[e]'

    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The Greek explicitly identifies the virgins as plural “holy spirits,” then as powers of the
      Son of God. That plural is retained. The draft does not replace them with the singular Holy Spirit
      or eliminate the garment/name image. “So” later in this paragraph is bracketed in the printed source.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The words from “of the tower” through “remaining in the building” are a long bar-marked insertion
      by Gebhardt compared with Latin Vulgata, Palatina and Ethiopic, reported absent in Athos by similar
      endings. Without it: “All the stones you saw in the building are clothed in the power of these virgins.”
      No Sinaiticus or Amherst fragment is claimed to preserve this entire supplied span.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “With” is bracketed in the working Greek, inserted by Hilgenfeld compared with the Latin traditions;
      Athos is reported to omit it, and Ethiopic differs. The draft retains the tower/rock unity without
      replacing the metaphor with a later theological formulation.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “And one garment” is bracketed in the printed source, as is the preceding introductory “he said.”
      The spirit, body and garment are kept distinct. The draft does not infer that the bracketed garment
      clause is legible in every witness.
  - marker: e
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: These women are allegorical figures whose names are supplied later in the vision. Their physical
      description and the exchange of powers remain in the narrative; the text is not generalized into
      a claim about women as a class.
